domain_characteristics.detection_complexity: high due to rarity, severe class imbalance, and subtle attack signatures especially in U2R and R2L categories
data_characteristics: includes connection, host behavior, and traffic pattern features

common_indicators: presence of root_shell=1 and num_root>0 indicating privilege escalation attempts
hot indicators > 0 signaling suspicious activity like system file access or program creation
high rerror_rate and srv_rerror_rate values (close to 1.0) indicating rejected connections or failed login attempts
flags such as RSTO and S3 associated with connection resets and suspicious session teardowns
low src_bytes with very high dst_bytes in some R2L attacks (e.g., warezmaster) indicating data exfiltration
logged_in=0 combined with num_failed_logins>0 indicating brute force or guessing attempts
attack_signatures: Signature 1: R2L attacks often have flag=RSTO or SF with high rerror_rate (≥0.9), num_failed_logins≥1, and logged_in=0, e.g., guess_passwd attack samples
Signature 2: U2R attacks show root_shell=1, hot≥1, logged_in=1, and increased num_compromised and num_root counts, often with short duration and service ftp_data or telnet

Signature 3: Warezmaster and warezclient attacks characterized by src_bytes=0, very large dst_bytes (millions), flag=SF, and same_srv_rate=1.0 indicating repeated access to the same service with no data sent from source
technical_markers: root_shell=1 and num_root≥1 as markers of privilege escalation
rerror_rate and srv_rerror_rate ≥0.9 as indicators of connection rejection/failure in R2L attacks
hot≥1 combined with logged_in=1 and num_compromised≥1 in U2R attacks
dst_bytes > 5,000,000 with src_bytes=0 in warezmaster attacks
serror_rate and srv_serror_rate near zero in most attacks except some guess_passwd samples with serror_rate≈0.5
attack_vectors: Remote-to-Local (R2L) via unauthorized login attempts and password guessing
User-to-Root (U2R) via privilege escalation exploiting vulnerabilities
Exploitation of FTP and Telnet services
Use of HTTP and IMAP services for remote attacks
exploit_techniques: Brute force login attempts indicated by num_failed_logins>0 and logged_in=0
Buffer overflow exploits causing root_shell=1 and hot indicators
Loadmodule and rootkit attacks manifesting as file creation and root access attempts
Data exfiltration via high dst_bytes with minimal src_bytes
Use of rejected connection flags and error rates to evade detection

typical_behaviors: Normal traffic predominantly uses protocol_type tcp, udp, and icmp with flag=SF
src_bytes and dst_bytes are balanced and moderate, with no extreme outliers
num_failed_logins=0 and logged_in=0 or 1 depending on session type
low or zero hot, num_compromised, root_shell, su_attempted, and num_root values
Stable connection patterns with high same_srv_rate (close to 1.0) and low error rates
baseline_metrics: serror_rate, srv_serror_rate, rerror_rate, srv_rerror_rate typically 0.0 in benign samples
count and srv_count can be high (e.g., 100+), reflecting normal repeated connections
dst_host_count and dst_host_srv_count often at maximum (255), indicating normal host activity
duration mostly 0 or low values, typical of normal short connections
hot=0 and num_failed_logins=0 in majority of benign samples
operational_patterns: Consistent use of service types like http, domain_u, eco_i, urp_i without error flags
Flags predominantly SF indicating successful connection establishment and teardown
Balanced src_bytes and dst_bytes indicating normal data exchange
Low or zero urgent and wrong_fragment counts
Stable host and service connection rates with low variability
normal_thresholds: serror_rate ≤ 0.1 and rerror_rate ≤ 0.1 for normal traffic
hot ≤ 0 and num_failed_logins = 0 for benign sessions
root_shell = 0 and num_root = 0 in normal activity
same_srv_rate ≥ 0.9 and diff_srv_rate ≤ 0.1 indicating service consistency
count and srv_count can be > 100 reflecting normal traffic bursts

current_threats: Rare and stealthy R2L attacks exploiting remote access to gain local privileges
U2R attacks focusing on privilege escalation to root access
Brute force password guessing attacks on Telnet and FTP services
Exploitation of common network services (ftp_data, telnet, http, imap4)
Use of rejected connection flags and error rates to evade detection
emerging_patterns: Increased use of high dst_bytes with zero src_bytes indicating data exfiltration
Subtle privilege escalation attempts with minimal hot indicators but root_shell=1
Frequent connection resets (RSTO flag) combined with high rerror_rate as evasion tactic
Service-specific error rate patterns (srv_serror_rate, srv_rerror_rate) as early warning signals
Low duration but high num_compromised and root_shell counts indicating fast exploitation
risk_factors: Severe class imbalance complicates detection and increases false negatives
Low visibility of U2R attacks due to subtle behavioral changes
High variability in service usage and connection flags
Potential for attackers to mimic normal traffic patterns
Dependence on multi-feature correlation for accurate detection
threat_landscape.threat_sophistication: high, involving stealthy privilege escalation, evasion via connection resets, and exploitation of multiple network services

detection_rules: Alert on root_shell=1 combined with hot≥1 and logged_in=1 indicating privilege escalation attempts
Flag connections with rerror_rate or srv_rerror_rate ≥ 0.9 and num_failed_logins≥1 with logged_in=0 as potential brute force R2L attacks
Detect warezmaster attacks by identifying src_bytes=0 with dst_bytes > 5,000,000 and same_srv_rate=1.0 on ftp_data service
Monitor for flags RSTO or S3 with high rerror_rate and srv_rerror_rate as indicators of suspicious connection resets
Correlate num_compromised and num_root counts with low duration sessions to detect fast exploitation
monitoring_recommendations: Continuous monitoring of login attempts and failed login counters
Track error rates (serror_rate, rerror_rate) at both connection and service levels
Analyze service usage patterns for anomalies in same_srv_rate and diff_srv_rate
Implement host behavior profiling focusing on root_shell and privilege escalation features
Use multi-feature anomaly detection models to capture subtle U2R and R2L attacks
threshold_suggestions: rerror_rate and srv_rerror_rate ≥ 0.9 for brute force detection
hot ≥ 1 combined with root_shell=1 for privilege escalation alerts
dst_bytes > 5,000,000 with src_bytes=0 for data exfiltration detection
serror_rate or srv_serror_rate > 0.5 in combination with failed logins for suspicious activity
same_srv_rate < 0.7 or diff_srv_rate > 0.3 as potential anomaly indicators
pattern_matching: Match sequences with repeated failed login attempts followed by logged_in=0 and high rerror_rate
Identify sessions with root_shell=1 and num_root>0 within short duration windows
Detect large data transfers with zero source bytes on ftp_data service
Correlate flag patterns (RSTO, S3) with error rates for connection reset attack detection
Use multi-dimensional pattern matching combining host behavior and network statistics for rare attack detection
